{{nihongo|'''Mitsuchino Shrine'''|蛟蝄神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimōsa Province]].

It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was {{ill|Q712534|lt=gōsha}}.

=== Overview ===
It stands in southern Ibaraki, on one part of the {{ill|Hitachi Plateau|Q102282520|qid=Q102282520}}. It is slightly south between Tone town center and {{ill|Ryūgasaki, Ibaraki|Q844138|qid=Q844138}} city center. The {{ill|Shin-Tone River|Q11501429|qid=Q11501429}} flows south of the shrine grounds.

It consists of two shrine buildings, Kado-no-miya and Oku-no-miya. The current Kado-no-miya honden was rebuilt in 1698 ({{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 11, {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}), and the Oku-no-miya honden in 1703 (Genroku 16). The Kado-no-miya honden is a Tone Town designated cultural property<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.town.tone.ibaraki.jp/kanko-bunka/rekisibunka/shiseki-bunkazai/page000161.html|title=Tone Town official site: Komo Shrine Kado-no-miya (left) / Oku-no-miya (right) |accessdate=2025-11-08}}</ref>.

The main deity is Mizuhanome-no-Ōkami, a water goddess governing water as the source of life. Many other deities, including Haniyamahime-no-Ōkami, are also {{ill|Co-Enshrinement|Q11412524|qid=Q11412524}} in the paired hall.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, it began in 288 BCE ({{ill|Emperor Kōrei|Q313041|qid=Q313041}} 3) with enshrinement of Mizuhanome-no-Ōkami at the present Kado-no-miya site. Later, in 698 CE ({{ill|Emperor Monmu|Q357246|qid=Q357246}} 2), Haniyamahime-no-Ōkami was enshrined in the paired hall and the buildings were restored<ref name=history>{{cite web |url=http://www.koumoujinja.jp/what_koumou.html|title=Komo Shrine official site|accessdate=2025-11-08}}</ref>.

In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, it was listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} as “Komo Shrine, one seat, Sōma District, {{ill|Shimōsa Province|ckb|پارێزگای شیمۆسا|cs|Provincie Šimósa|de|Provinz Shimousa|es|Provincia de Shimōsa|fa|ولایت شیموسا|fr|Province de Shimōsa|gl|Provincia de Shimōsa|hak|Shimōsa-koet|id|Provinsi Shimousa|it|Shimōsa|ja|下総国|ko|시모사국|lt|Šimosos žemė|nl|Shimosa (provincie)|pt|Província de Shimōsa|ru|Симоса (провинция)|simple|Shimōsa Province|sk|Šimósa|sr|Провинција Шимоса|tr|Shimōsa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сімоса|zh|下總國|zh_min_nan|Simôsa-kok|zh_yue|下總國|qid=Q1053695}},” and was ranked a shikinaisha<ref name=history></ref>.

From the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} onward it was also called “Bumma Daimyōjin,” gathering faith as a local water deity. Since the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it has inherited worship for rain-prayer, rain-stopping, and abundant harvest as the “oldest water-deity shrine in {{ill|Kantō|Q11655841|qid=Q11655841}},” and remains revered as a local guardian deity<ref name=history></ref>.
